extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (computational algebraists, mathematicians using SINGULAR libraries)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance, assumptions, options and return-value behavior for SINGULAR library procedures (mregular.lib, noether.lib, normal.lib) used for tests like Noether position, nested ideals, satiety/regularity, normalization, Hom computations, genus and prime-closure computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: is_NP — Assumption (Noether position test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assume: i is a nonzero proper homogeneous ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in procedures regIdeal, depthIdeal, satiety, and NoetherPosition. Note/example: If i is not homogeneous and NP(i)=1 then K[x(n-d+1),...,x(n)] is a Noether normalization of S/i. The converse may be wrong if the ideal is not homogeneous.

rubrics_metrics.name: is_nested — Monomial nested-type test
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is_nested(i); i monomial ideal. Return: 1 if i is of nested type, 0 otherwise. (returns -1 if i=(0) or i=(1)). Assume: i is a nonzero proper monomial ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1. The ideal must be monomial, otherwise the result has no meaning (so check this before using this procedure). 2. is_nested is used in procedures depthIdeal, regIdeal and satiety. 3. When i is a monomial ideal of nested type of S=K[x(0)..x(n)], the a-invariant of S/i coincides with the upper bound obtained using the procedure regIdeal with printlevel > 0. An ideal is of nested type if its associated primes are all of the form a monomial (x(0),...,x(i)) for some i<=n (see referenced preprint for the effective criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: NPos_test — Noether position monomial test
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: NPos_test(I); I monomial ideal. Return: A list whose first element is 1, if i is in Noether position, 0 otherwise. The second element of this list is a list of variables ordered such that those variables are listed first, of which a power belongs to the initial ideal of i. If i is in Noether position, the method returns furthermore the dimension of i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: i is a nonzero monomial ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: modNpos_test — Probabilistic Noether position test
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: modNpos_test(i); i an ideal. Return: 1 if i is in Noether position 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This test is a probabilistic test, and it computes the initial of the ideal modulo the prime number 2147483647 (the biggest prime less than 2^31).

rubrics_metrics.name: NPos — Construct linear map to Noether position
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: NPos(i); i ideal. Return: A linear map phi such that phi(i) is in Noether position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deterministic transformation to put ideal into Noether position (no probabilistic note here).

rubrics_metrics.name: modNPos — Probabilistic linear map to Noether position
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: modNPos(i); i ideal. Return: A linear map phi such that phi(i) is in Noether position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It uses the procedure modNPos test to test Noether position (probabilistic; works via computation modulo the prime 2147483647).

rubrics_metrics.name: nsatiety — Satiety (saturation index) computation
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: nsatiety(i); i ideal. Return: an integer, the satiety of i. (returns -1 if i is not homogeneous). Assume: i is a homogeneous ideal of the basering R=K[x(0)..x(n)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: The satiety, or saturation index, of a homogeneous ideal i is the least integer s such that, for all d>=s, the degree d part of the ideals i and isat=sat(i,maxideal(1))[1] coincide.

rubrics_metrics.name: modsatiety — Probabilistic satiety computation
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: modsatiety(i); i ideal. Return: an integer, the satiety of i. (returns -1 if i is not homogeneous). Assume: i is a homogeneous ideal of the basering R=K[x(0)..x(n)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a probabilistic procedure, and it computes the initial of the ideal modulo the prime number 2147483647 (the biggest prime less than 2^31).

rubrics_metrics.name: regCM — Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity (deterministic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: regCM(i); i ideal. Return: the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of i. (returns -1 if i is not homogeneous). Assume: i is a homogeneous ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deterministic computation; returns -1 for non-homogeneous ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: modregCM — Probabilistic Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: modregCM(i); i ideal. Return: an integer, the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of i. (returns -1 if i is not homogeneous).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: i is a homogeneous ideal and the characteristic of base field is zero. Note: This is a probabilistic procedure, and it computes the initial of the ideal modulo the prime number 2147483647 (the biggest prime less than 2^31).

rubrics_metrics.name: normal — Normalization of affine rings (general algorithm)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: normal(id [,choose]); id = radical ideal, choose = list of options. Return: a list nor (size 2 or 3 with 'withDelta') describing normalization rings, module generators and optionally delta invariants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional parameters in choose: Decomposition options: 'equidim' (default), 'prim', 'noDeco', 'isPrim'. Other options: 'noFac', 'useRing', 'withDelta' (or 'wd'), list('inputJ', ideal inputJ), list('inputC', ideal inputC), 'var1', 'var2'. Assume: The ideal must be radical (id=radical(id) will make it radical). Note: 'isPrim' should only be used if id is known to be prime. Implementation works also for local rings. Not implemented for quotient rings. If input ideal is weighted homogeneous a weighted ordering may be used together with the useRing-option (qhweight(id) computes weights). nor[1] contains rings Ri with ideals norid and normap; nor[2] gives R-module generators; nor[3] (with 'withDelta') gives delta invariants. Increasing/decreasing printlevel displays more/less comments (default: printlevel=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: normalP — Positive-characteristic normalization (Frobenius-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: normalP(id [,choose]); id = radical ideal, choose = optional list of strings. Return: a list nor of size 2 (or 3 if 'withRing' is set) giving module or ring structure and delta invariants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional parameters: 'withRing', 'isPrim', 'noFac', 'noRed'. Assume: The characteristic of the ground field must be positive. If 'isPrim' is set the ideal must be prime otherwise the result may be wrong. If 'isPrim' not set minimal associated primes are computed first and normalP computes the normalization of the radical of id. Not implemented for local or mixed orderings or quotient rings; for local or mixed orderings use proc 'normal'. If the input ideal is weighted homogeneous a weighted ordering may be used. normalP uses the Leonard-Pellikaan-Singh-Swanson algorithm (Frobenius-based). nor[1] (when 'withRing') gives rings Ri with norid and normap; nor[2] gives module generators; nor[3] gives delta invariants (-1 means infinite, 0 normal).

rubrics_metrics.name: normalC — Normalization computing algebra generators (Grauert-Remmert-de Jong)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: normalC(id [,choose]); id = radical ideal, choose = optional list of strings. Return: a list nor (size 2 or 3) giving rings, module/generator ideals, and delta invariants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional parameters: 'equidim', 'prim', 'noDeco', 'isPrim', 'noFac', 'withGens'. Assume: The ideal must be radical (id=radical(id) makes id radical). If 'prim' is set minimal associated primes are computed first. 'isPrim' should only be used if id is known to be irreducible. If 'withGens' not set nor[2] shows delta invariants; if 'withGens' set nor[2] is a list of ideals Ii generating the integral closure as K-algebra; nor[3] shows delta invariants. Theory: uses Grauert-Remmert-de Jong algorithm. Not implemented for local or mixed orderings or quotient rings; for those use 'normal'. If input ideal is weighted homogeneous, a weighted ordering may be used. Increasing printlevel displays more/less comments (default: printlevel=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: HomJJ — Compute End_R(J) (endomorphism ring) and map R -> End_R(J)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: HomJJ(Li); Li = list: ideal SBid, ideal id, ideal J, poly p. Assume: R = P/id, P = basering (polynomial ring), id an ideal of P, SBid = standard basis of id, J = ideal of P containing the polynomial p, p = nonzero divisor of R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: Endomorphism ring End_R(J)=Hom_R(J,J) with its ring structure as affine ring, together with the map R -> Hom_R(J,J). Return: list l with l[1] a polynomial ring containing ideals 'endid' and 'endphi' such that l[1]/endid = Hom_R(J,J) and endphi describes canonical map R -> Hom_R(J,J); l[2] integer 1 if phi is an isomorphism, 0 if not; l[3] integer = dim_K(Hom_R(J,J)/R) (finite or -1). Note: printlevel >=1 displays comments (default: printlevel=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: genus — Geometric genus of projective curve
rubrics_metrics.description: Return: an integer, the geometric genus p_g = p_a - delta of the projective curve defined by i, where p_a is the arithmetic genus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: genus always treats projective curves and takes projective closure if input is affine 1-dim variety. delta is the sum of all local delta-invariants of the singularities, i.e. dim(R'/R) where R' is normalization of local ring R of the singularity. genus(I,'nor') uses the normalization to compute delta (usually slower). genus(I,'pri') starts with a primary decomposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: primeClosure — Sequence of rings approximating integral closure
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: primeClosure(L [,c]); L a list of a ring containing a prime ideal ker, c an optional integer. Return: a list L (of size n+1) consisting of rings L[1],...,L[n] such that L[1] is a copy of the input ring, L[n]/ker is the integral closure of L[1]/ker in its quotient field, and L[n+1] is the delta invariant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: L is constructed by recursive calls of primeClosure itself. c determines the choice of nzd (non-zero divisor): c not given or equal to 0: first generator of the ideal SL, the singular locus of Spec(L[i]/ker); c<>0: the generator of SL with least number of monomials. L[i] contain polynomials nzd so that elements of L[i]/ker are quotients of elements of L[i-1]/ker with denominator nzd via the injection phi.
